usual_baseline: Falls risk assessment itself is usually done well: 97.3% on admission [1169], 93% [1487]. The weak items are the checks that follow it. Lying and standing BP was done in only 32% [1392] and 34% [1487]. Fracture checks were 60.3% and neurological observations 75% [1169]. Medication review within 4 weeks of a fall in primary care was 22% [1547].
fix_that_works: Education on lying and standing BP, with flyers, aide-memoires and huddle reminders: 32% to 83.3% [1392] and 34% to 68% [1487]. SystmOne prompts, clinician education and weekly MDT fall reviews raised medication review from 22% to 94% [1547]. A corrective action plan improved nearly all criteria; staff education rose by 46% and patient and family education by 43% [1297].
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. Falls assessment barely moved, from 93% to 98% (p = 0.61), because it was already high [1487]. LSBP was sometimes ticked as done on the falls form when it was not [1487].
consultant_advice: Auditing whether a falls risk form was completed is overdone; it is nearly always above 90%. Measure lying and standing BP, post-fall medication review, and fracture and neurological checks after a fall. Check the actual BP readings, not the tick box.
